html:
SMTO-AUT-0034 — Your Google account changed while SMTO was using it

GUID: 8635be3e-ba8a-5ef7-9c89-c135a6ff942a
Slug: google-account-changed
Domain: AUT · Subsystem: google-workspace

What happened

  • The saved Google account this action relies on was changed, removed or reconnected partway through. SMTO stopped instead of quietly switching accounts, and it didn't save a new sign-in or send this request using the changed account.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the Task was changing something in Google, such as adding a calendar event or uploading a file, first check Google Calendar or Google Drive to see whether it already happened. Steps before the account changed may have finished, and repeating them could create duplicates.
  2. Open Parameter Store from the More options menu and find your Google Workspace Account entry. Check it is the Google account you expect, and don't edit it while a Task uses it. SMTO stops whenever this entry is removed, recreated or reconnected as a different person during an action.
  3. If you were connecting Google, ask SMTO to connect the account again and finish Google's sign-in page within ten minutes, without running other Google Tasks meanwhile. SMTO only saves a sign-in if the account entry hasn't changed since the sign-in link was created.
  4. Then ask again in a new message. If you have more than one Google account, pick the one you want by typing @ and its Parameter Store name. Naming the account makes SMTO use exactly that account instead of choosing one for you.

What success looks like

  • The Google request finishes and its result names the Google account you expected.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO's Google setup. Don't delete and recreate the Google Workspace Account entry to force it through; that removes the connection and stops running Tasks the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Google Workspace account record changed (created_at, subject, oauth_app_ref or updated_at revision) between account selection and its use in consent completion, token refresh or a Calendar/Drive request, so SMTO refused to continue.

What this means

  • Accepted account identity or a compare-and-save revision changed while selection, refresh, consent or a consumer request was in progress. Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.

Why this can happen

  • Accepted account identity or a compare-and-save revision changed while selection, refresh, consent or a consumer request was in progress.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare retained account identity, app reference and record revisions with the current Parameter Store entry.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the google_account record in Parameter Store (subject, oauth_app_ref, created_at, updated_at) and any accepted @-reference in the conversation; the error comes from resolve_account binding checks, the GoogleProfiles.save_tokens compare-and-update guard, or the CalendarClient/DriveClient expected_identity check. Confirm the intended identity and whether earlier writes completed, then restart consent with auth.google_connect using the same account_key or rerun the read; never substitute another account.
  • Inspect the current account and application in Parameter Store, then restart consent or retry the read operation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm account identity and required features before retrying.

How to verify the fix

  • A fresh selection or consent uses the current unchanged intended account identity.

What not to do

  • Do not expose client secrets, tokens, codes or PKCE verifiers.
  • Do not switch accounts or repeat uncertain mutations automatically.

Technical notes

  • Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
